title: Sourdough Schedule — a backward bake planner
description: A sourdough planner that works backwards from the moment you want bread out of the oven. You set kitchen and dough temperatures, starter strength and your formula, and it builds a timeline: starter feed, levain, autolyse, mix, four stretch-and-folds, bulk, shaping, cold retard, preheat and bake. Fermentation times come from a clearly labelled rule-of-thumb temperature model. Steps between 11 PM and 6 AM are flagged and can be avoided with one tap, a baker's-percentage calculator handles the levain's own flour and water correctly, and the schedule prints cleanly.
prompt: Build me a sourdough bake planner. I pick when I want bread out of the oven, the dough and kitchen temperatures, starter strength and hydration, and it backward-schedules the whole thing: feed, levain, autolyse, mix, stretch-and-folds, bulk, shape, cold retard, bake. Use a rule-of-thumb temperature model for fermentation time and label it as one. Include a baker's-percentage recipe calculator with correct math (count the levain's flour and water) and make the schedule printable. Bonus points if it warns me before scheduling a fold at 3 AM.

methodology: Math oracle for the formula: for a 1,000 g dough at 75% hydration, 20% levain and 2% salt, the spec derives total flour (1000 / 1.77) and each ingredient independently. It checks the rendered grams, that flour and water inside the levain are counted toward the totals, and that the ingredients sum to the dough weight.
Model checks against the labelled rule: 5 h 00 min at 76°F, 2^(12/14) × 5 h at 64°F, 4 h 15 min with a vigorous starter, a 6 h 06 min levain at 72°F, and clamping at 2.5 h and 14 h.

Backward-scheduling oracle: with page.clock fixed, every step's data-time is compared to its exact minute offset from the bake (45, 105, 12 h + 45, …), including fold spacing, autolyse lead and the 12 h starter feed. A longer retard must shift every earlier step by the same amount.
Night logic: a 2 PM bake with a 12 h retard puts three or more steps between 11 PM and 6 AM, and 'Avoid night-time steps' must find a retard with zero, which the test verifies on every step's hour.
A bake time too soon to start is caught, and 'Soonest possible bake' starts the plan 10–26 minutes after the fake 'now'.

Units and print: °C readouts convert correctly and feed the same model; window.print is stubbed to count calls, and emulateMedia({ media: 'print' }) hides the controls, buttons and chart while keeping the steps, recipe and print header.
risks: Time zones and DST: all maths is in epoch milliseconds and only formatted locally; the tests compare offsets rather than wall-clock strings, except where the fake clock pins the date.
Baker's percentages are easy to get subtly wrong (hydration including or excluding the levain); the page states its convention and the test checks both totals.
datetime-local support and parsing differ between browsers; values are parsed as local time and invalid input is ignored.
Emoji step icons render differently by platform; one that Windows 10 can't draw was replaced, and on narrow screens the icons are hidden.
qa.playwright: Time is the whole product here, so each scheduling test starts with page.clock.install() and pauseAt() on a known Thursday noon. That makes the default bake date, the 'too soon' check and the 'soonest bake' rounding fully deterministic. Step times are asserted from each step's machine-readable data-time attribute as minute offsets, which avoids locale formatting, and a few human-readable labels are spot-checked. The print path uses two techniques: window.print is replaced with a counter to prove the button calls it, and page.emulateMedia({ media: 'print' }) checks the @media print rules. The fermentation model is exposed on window.__dough so the spec can confirm the clamps without driving sliders to extreme values.
coverage: Baker's-percentage grams, totals, whole-wheat split, multiple loaves
Temperature and starter-strength model with clamps
Exact backward offsets for every step; retard change; optional starter feed
Night-step flagging and avoidance; too-soon warning; soonest possible bake
Celsius conversion; print button and print stylesheet

a11y: All inputs are native and labelled: a datetime-local field, range sliders with visible outputs, number fields and a checkbox. Units and starter strength are toggle buttons with aria-pressed. The warning line is aria-live, the timeline chart has a descriptive aria-label, the steps are an ordered list with machine-readable <time> elements, and the recipe is a real table.
